sanskrit:
[Origin of marutsVishala constructs the city Diti practises her austerities--Sumati  honours Viswamitra.]
सप्तधातु कृते गर्भे दिति: परमदु:खिता।
सहस्राक्षं दुराधर्षं वाक्यं सानुनयाऽब्रवीत्।।1.47.1।।
word_by_word: गर्भे when the embryo, सप्तधा into seven pieces,  कृते having been cut, दिति: Diti, परमदु:खिता highly distressed, दुराधर्षम् unassailable, सहस्राक्षम् Indra, सानुनया affectionate, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Deeply distressed Diti, having come to know that the embryo had been severed into seven pieces, humbly spoke to the unassailable Indra.

sanskrit:
ममापराधाद्गर्भोऽयं सप्तधा विफलीकृत:।
नापराधोऽस्ति देवेश तवात्र बलसूदन।।1.47.2।।
word_by_word: बलसूदन O Slayer of Balasura, देवेश Devendra, मम my, अपराधात् by the fault, अयम् this,  गर्भ: embryo, सप्तधा into seven pieces, विफलीकृत: rendered useless, अत्र in this matter, तव your, अपराध: fault, नास्ति was not there.
explanation:
"O Indra, Slayer of Balasura, because of my fault this embryo has been made into
seven pieces and rendered useless. In this matter you have not committed any fault.

sanskrit:
प्रियं तु कर्तुमिच्छामि मम गर्भविपर्यये।
मरुतां सप्तसप्तानां स्थानपाला भवन्त्विमे।।1.47.3।।
word_by_word: गर्भविपर्यये this misfortune to embryo, मम for me, प्रियम् favour, कर्तुम् to do, इच्छामि I am desiring, इमे this, सप्त seven pieces, सप्तानां seven, मरुताम् maruts, स्थानपाला guardians of regions, भवन्तु become.
explanation: This disaster to the embryo has happened contrary to expectations. Hence, I seek a favour from you. Let these seven pieces become seven guardians of marut regions (regions of the wind).

sanskrit: वातस्कन्धा: इमे सप्त चरन्तु दिवि पुत्रक ।

ब्रह्मलोकं चरत्वेक इन्द्रलोकं तथाऽपर:।
दिवि वायुरिति ख्यातस्तृतीयोऽपि महायशा:।।1.47.5।।
word_by_word: एक: one, ब्रह्मलोकम् in Brahma loka, चरतु may move about, तथा similarly, अपर: another, इन्द्रलोकम् Indra loka, महायशा: highly renowned, तृतीयोऽपि third one, वायुरिति known as Vayu, ख्यात: wellknown, दिवि in this universe, move about.
explanation: Among them, one will move about in Brahmaloka, another in Indraloka, and the third, well known as vayu will move around in the sky.

sanskrit:
चत्वारस्तु सुरश्रेष्ठ दिशो वै तव शासनात्।
सञ्चरिष्यन्तु भद्रं ते देवभूता ममात्मजा:।।1.47.6।।
word_by_word: सुरश्रेष्ठ O Best of devatas, चत्वार: four, मम आत्मजा: my  sons, तव your, शासनात् by command, देवभूता: becoming celestial beings, दिश: directions, सञ्चरिष्यन्तु may range about.
explanation: O best of devatas by your command the other four sons will remain celestial, and will range about in four directions.

sanskrit:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सहस्राक्ष: पुरन्दर:।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं दितिं बलनिषूदन:।।1.47.7।।
word_by_word: सहस्राक्ष: thousandeyed, बलनिषूदन: slayer of Bala, पुरन्दर: Indra, तस्या: her, तत् वचनम् those words, शृत्वा having heard, प्राञ्जलि: with folded palms, दितिम् addressing Diti, वाक्यम् these words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: The thousandeyed Indra, slayer of Bala, on hearing Diti's words, addressed her with folded palms, saying:

sanskrit:
सर्वमेतद्यथोक्तं ते भविष्यति न संशय:।
विचरिष्यन्ति भद्रं ते देवभूतास्तवात्मजा:।।1.47.8।।
word_by_word: ते to you, यथा as, उक्तम् said, एतत् सर्वम् all this, भविष्यति will take place, संशय: doubt, न not there, तव your, आत्मजा: sons, देवभूता: like celestial beings, विचरिष्यन्ति shall wander about, भद्रम् ते prosperity to you.
explanation: "Everything will, no doubt, happen the way you said. Your sons will wander about as celestial beings. Prosperity to you."

sanskrit:
एवं तौ निश्चयं कृत्वा मातापुत्रौ तपोवने।
जग्मतुस्त्रिदिवं राम कृतार्थाविति नश्श्रुतम्।।1.47.9।।
word_by_word: राम O Rama, तौ मातापुत्रौ those mother and sons, एवम् in this way, निश्चयम् conclusion, कृत्वा having arrived, कृतार्थौ having fulfilled their desire, त्रिदिवम् towords heaven, जग्मतु: had gone, इति श्रुतम् thus heard.
explanation: "O Rama mother and sons having arrived at this conclusion in the tapovana  ascended to heaven with their desire fulfilled. This is what we have heard."

sanskrit:
एष देशस्स काकुत्स्थ महेन्द्राध्युषित: पुरा।
दितिं यत्र तपस्सिद्धामेवं परिचचार स:।।1.47.10।।
word_by_word: काकुत्स्थ O Rama, एष: this one, पुरा formerly, महेन्द्राध्युषित: inhabited by Indra, स: that, देश: country, यत्र where, स: he, तप: in austerities, सिद्धाम् succeded, दितिम् Diti, एवम् this way, परिचचार attended on.
explanation: "O Descendant of Kakustha (Rama) this is that country which was formerly inhabited by Indra. Here Indra  attended on Diti who achieved the fruit of her austerities.

sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकोऽस्तु नरव्याघ्र पुत्र: परमधार्मिक:।।1.47.11।।
अलम्बुषायामुत्पन्नो विशाल इति विश्रुत:।
तेन चासीदिह स्थाने विशालेति पुरी कृता।।1.47.12।।
word_by_word: नरव्याघ्र O Tiger among men, Rama, इक्ष्वाको: for Ikshvaku, अलम्बुषायाम् in Alambusa, परमधार्मिक: highly virtuous, विशाल इति named Vishala, विश्रुत: wellknown, पुत्र: son, उत्पन्न: was norn, तेन by him, इह here, स्थाने in this place, विशालेति named as Vishala, पुरी city, कृता आसीत् was built.
explanation: "O Tiger among men (Rama) this highly virtuous and wellknown son named Vishala was born to Ikshvakus in Alambusa. Where, a city named Vishala was built.

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकोऽस्तु नरव्याघ्र पुत्र: परमधार्मिक:।।1.47.11।।

विशालस्य सुतो राम हेमचन्द्रो महाबल:।
सुचन्द्र इति विख्यात: हेमचन्द्रादनन्तर:।।1.47.13।।
word_by_word: राम O Rama, महाबल: mighty, हेमचन्द्र: Hemachandra, विशालस्य Vishala's, सुत: son, हेमचन्द्रात् from Hemachandra, अनन्तर: his successor, सुचन्द्र इति as Suchandra, विख्यात: celebrated one.
explanation: O Rama mighty Hemachandra was Vishala's son. Hemachandra's successor was the celebrated Suchandra.

sanskrit:
सुचन्द्रतनयो राम धूम्राश्व इति विश्रुत:।
धूम्राश्वतनयश्चापि सञ्जयस्समपद्यत।।1.47.14।।
word_by_word: राम O Rama, सुचन्द्रतनय: son of Suchandra, धूम्राश्व इति as Dhumraswa, विश्रुत: wellknown, सञ्जय: Sanjaya, धूम्राश्वतनय: son of Dhumraswa, समपद्यत was born.
explanation: O Rama son of Suchandra was Dhumraswa, wellknown Sanjaya was the son of Dhumraswa.

sanskrit:
सञ्जयस्य सुतश्श्रीमान् सहदेव: प्रतापवान्।
कुशाश्वस्सहदेवस्य पुत्र: परमधार्मिक:।।1.47.15।।
word_by_word: श्रीमान् prosperous, प्रतापवान् powerful, सहदेव: Sahadeva, सञ्जयस्य Sanjaya's, सुत: son, परमधार्मिक: highly virtuous, कुशाश्व: Kusaswa, सहदेवस्य Sahadeva's, पुत्र: son.
explanation: Prosperous and powerful Sahadeva was Sanjaya's son. Highly virtuous Kusaswa was Sahadeva's son.

sanskrit:
कुशाश्वस्य महातेजा सोमदत्त: प्रतापवान्।
सोमदत्तस्य पुत्रस्तु काकुत्स्थ इति विश्रुत:।।1.47.16।।
word_by_word: महातेजा: highly lustrous, प्रतापवान् powerful, सोमदत्त: Somadatta, कुशाश्वस्य Kusaswa's (son), सोमदत्तस्य Somadatta's, पुत्र: son, काकुत्स्थ: Kakutstha, इति विश्रुत: is wellknown.
explanation: Brilliant and powerful Somadatta was Kusaswa's son. That Somadatta's son was Kakutstha is wellknown.

sanskrit:
तस्य पुत्रो महातेजा: सम्प्रत्येष पुरीमिमाम्।
आवसत्यमरप्रख्यस्सुमतिर्नाम दुर्जय:।।1.47.17।।
word_by_word: सम्प्रति now, इमां पुरीम् in this city, तस्य पुत्र: son of Ikshvaku, महातेजा: heroic, अमरप्रख्य: equal to devatas, दुर्जय: invincible, सुमतिर्नाम named Sumati, आवसति is living.
explanation: Son of Ikshvakus, Sumati comparable to devatas, invincible and exceedingly energetic is still ruling this city.

sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकोस्तु प्रसादेन सर्वे वैशालिका नृपा:।
दीर्घायुषो महात्मानो वीर्यवन्तस्सुधार्मिका:।।1.47.18।।
word_by_word: इक्ष्वाको: Ikshwaku's, प्रसादेन by his graciousness, वैशालिका: relating to Vishala, नृपा: kings, सर्वे all, दीर्घायुष: possessing longlife, महात्मान: exalted, वीर्यवन्त: valourous, सुधार्मिका: are virtuous.
explanation: By the grace of the Ikshvakus, all the kings of Vishala have been long lived and exalted, valiant and deeply religious.

sanskrit:
इहाद्य रजनीं राम सुखं वत्स्यामहे वयम्।
श्व: प्रभाते नरश्रेष्ठ जनकं द्रष्टुमर्हसि।।1.47.19।।
word_by_word: राम O Rama, अद्य today, रजनीम् night, वयम् we, इह here, सुखम् happily, वत्स्यामहे will stay on, नरश्रेष्ठ O Best among men, श्व: tomorrow, प्रभाते early morning, जनकम् Janaka, द्रष्टुम् to see, अर्हसि fit and proper.
explanation: O Rama we shall spend the right happily here. O Best among men On the tomorrow we see Janaka".

sanskrit:
सुमतिस्तु महातेजा विश्वामित्रमुपागतम्।
श्रुत्वा नरवरश्रेष्ठ: प्रत्युद्गच्छन्महायशा:।।1.47.20।।
word_by_word: महातेजा: most brilliant, महायशा: man of immense renown, नरवरश्रेष्ठ: chief of men, सुमतिस्तु king Sumati, विश्वामित्रम् Visvamitra, उपागतम् arrived, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रत्युद्गच्छत् went forward (to receive him).
explanation: Having heard of the arrival of Viswamitra the celebrated Sumati, most brilliant chief of kings proceeded (to receive him).

sanskrit:
पूजां च परमां कृत्वा सोपाध्यायस्सबान्धव:।
प्राञ्जलि: कुशलं पृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्।।1.47.21।।
word_by_word: सोपाध्याय: with spiritual preceptors, सबान्धव: together with  his relatives, परमाम् supreme, पूजाम् honours, कृत्वा having performed, प्राञ्जलि: with folded palms, कुशलम् welfare, पृष्ट्वा having enquired, अथ thereafter, विश्वामित्रम् addressing Visvamitra, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation:
Along with his spiritual preceptors and relatives he paid Viswamitra great respect,
enquired his wellbeing and said:

sanskrit:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे विषयं मुनि:।
सम्प्राप्तो दर्शनं चैव नास्ति धन्यतरो मम।।1.47.22।।
word_by_word: यस्य मे my, विषयम् country, मुनि: Muni (you), सम्प्राप्त: has visited, दर्शनम् चैव having graced all of us, धन्य: अस्मि blessed am I, अनुगृहीत: अस्मि I am ( highly )favoured, मम for me, न अस्ति धन्यतर: there is none more blessed than me.
explanation:
"O Sage no one is more blessed than me since you have favoured me with your arrival in my country."
इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशस्सर्ग:।।
Thus ends the fortyseventh sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
